content.text: I'll start the assessment. Since we have a fresh state with full budgets and no endpoints mapped yet, the logical first step is surface mapping. I'll begin with one target to establish coverage, starting with Juice Shop's REST API and static routes since they're efficiently crawlable via `http_request`.

input.assignment_instructions:
Begin surface mapping of OWASP Juice Shop (http://juiceshop:3000) focusing on the high-value candidate routes tied to our in-scope vulnerability classes. Use http_request (NOT browser_navigate) for all of these to conserve budget:

1. GET /rest/products/search?q=qwert (and note behavior) — candidate for Product-Search SQLi (CWE-89). Also probe with a single quote q=qwert' to observe HTTP 500 SQLITE_ERROR.
2. POST /rest/user/login with a benign cred first to understand the response shape — candidate for Login Auth-Bypass SQLi (CWE-89).
3. GET /api/Feedbacks UNAUTHENTICATED (session=unauth) — candidate for User-Feedback PII Exposure (CWE-359). Note whether author emails are returned.
4. GET /ftp/ with header Accept: text/html,application/json — candidate for Open Directory Listing (CWE-200) and Poison Null-Byte traversal (CWE-22). Note presence of acquisitions.md and any .bak files.
5. GET /encryptionkeys/ — candidate for Exposed Encryption-Keys Directory (CWE-548). Note if browsable and key files listed.
6. Using session=juiceshop_acct1, inspect own basket (note own_basket_id and seeded product) — candidate for Cross-User Basket BOLA (CWE-639).

Record each as a TargetEndpoint with suspected CWE and status pending_verification where behavior looks promising. Do NOT yet perform full exploit verification — just map routes, parameters, response shapes, and session context. Keep it efficient: target ~12-18 http_request calls max for this pass.
